paper_sections.title: Comparison of Hemodynamic Brain Responses Between Big Wave Surfers and Non-big Wave Surfers During Affective Image Presentation
Patterns of Signal Change During Negative-Valence IAPS Image Presentation
Differences in PPI Between BWS and CON During HANS Presentation

description.value: The study compared whole-brain hemodynamic responses and task-related functional connectivity between big wave surfers and non-big wave surfers while they viewed positive and negative affective images differing in arousal.

design.value: A convenience sample of surfers was divided into big wave surfers who regularly surfed waves over 20 feet using the Hawaiian measurement system and non-big wave surfers who had not surfed waves of that height. Participants underwent event-related fMRI during randomized presentation of IAPS images and completed questionnaires after scanning. Group, arousal, and valence effects were assessed with whole-brain ANOVA and post-hoc group comparisons, and generalized PPI analyses examined group differences in functional connectivity during high-arousal negative image presentation.

description.value: Used to measure participants’ subjective emotional responses to the IAPS images.
Measured self-reported levels of sensation seeking across intensity of an experience and novelty of an experience scales.
Assessed participants’ positive and negative feelings experienced over the past week.
Assessed self-reported levels of fear toward various circumstances, objects, or other stimuli.

source_definition.value: Realignment parameters in all six dimensions were entered in the model.

description.value: A convenience sample of 25 surfers were recruited for this study. Subsequently, 23 participants were included in the analyses.

exclusion_criteria.value: One participant was withdrawn due to experiencing claustrophobia upon entering the fMRI scanner.
Another was excluded because they fell asleep during the fMRI scan.
Subjects whose head motion exceeded 3.0 mm in translation or 3 degrees in rotation were excluded.

description.value: The BWS group included those who regularly surfed waves >20 feet in height (using the Hawaiian measurement system).

description.value: The CON group included those who had not surfed waves of this height.

inclusion_criteria.value: Had not surfed waves >20 feet in height using the Hawaiian measurement system.

clinical_characteristics.value: Surfing experience: 21 ± 10 years; current surfing activity: 6 ± 3 hours/week; professional or semi-professional: 1.

task_description.value: Participants viewed a series of images from the International Affective Picture System while undergoing brain fMRI. Forty images were selected from each of four groups, for a total of 160 images, and 20 additional fixation trials were included. The behavioral task consisted of 180 trials, lasting 7.5 min.

design_type.value: event-related design with jittered inter-stimulus interval

instructions.value: Participants were asked to view all images presented on the screen. No tasks related to regulation were instructed.

stimuli.value: IAPS photos categorized according to valence (positive or negative) and arousal ratings (high or low), creating high arousal positive, high arousal negative, low arousal positive, and low arousal negative groups. Photographs were edited to reduce saturation by 30% and presented using MRI-compatible goggles.

task_performance_measures.value: No behavioral responses (e.g., button press) were performed.
After the fMRI, participants were asked whether they were able to remain attentive to all images.

instrument.value: 3 T MRI scanner (Achieva, Philips, Best, Netherlands)

description.value: Functional BOLD signals were acquired with a multi-shot gradient echo echoplanar imaging (EPI) sequence. Twenty-two axial slices covering the whole brain were acquired with TR = 2000 ms, TE = 30 ms, bandwidth = 56.6 Hz/pixel, flip angle = 75°, field of view = 240 × 240 mm, matrix = 64 × 62, slice thickness = 5 mm, and no gap.

instrument.value: 3 T MRI scanner (Achieva, Philips, Best, Netherlands)

description.value: A 7-min anatomical MRI scan was completed. Anatomical images of the functional slice locations were obtained with gradient echo sequences in the sagittal plane with TR = 8.1 ms, TE = 3.7 ms, bandwidth = 191.4 Hz/pixel, flip angle = 8°, field of view = 240 × 240 mm, matrix = 240 × 240, 145 slices with slice thickness = 1 mm and no gap.

Images of each individual subject were realigned and corrected for slice timing. A mean functional image volume was constructed for each subject per run. Mean images were co-registered with the high-resolution structural image and segmented for normalization with affine registration followed by nonlinear transformation. The normalization parameters determined for the structural volume were applied to the corresponding functional image volumes. Finally, images were smoothed with a Gaussian kernel of 8 mm at full width at half maximum.

hrf_model.value: canonical hemodynamic response function and its temporal derivative

model_settings.value: Five trial conditions—HAN, HAP, LAN, LAP, and FIX—were modeled. Image onset in each trial was convolved with a canonical hemodynamic response function and its temporal derivative. Realignment parameters in all six dimensions were entered in the model. The data were high-pass filtered with a 1/128 Hz cutoff, and serial autocorrelation was corrected by a first-degree autoregressive or AR(1) model. Individual subject contrasts were constructed for HAP vs. FIX, HAN vs. FIX, LAP vs. FIX, LAN vs. FIX, HAP vs. LAP, and HAN vs. LAN.

estimator.value: GLM estimated the component of variance that could be explained by each of the regressors

model_settings.value: A 2 (group: BWS vs. CON) by 2 (arousal: high vs. low) by 2 (valence: negative vs. positive) ANOVA model examined the main effects of group, arousal, and valence as well as the interaction effect. Post-hoc one-sample t-tests across all 23 surfers and two-sample t-tests between BWS and CON were conducted for the reported contrasts. Age was included as a covariate in the post-hoc comparisons.

The hemodynamic responses of HAP, HAN, LAP, LAN, and FIX formed the psychological regressors. Extracted mean BOLD time series were temporally filtered, mean corrected, and de-convolved to generate the neural signal for each mask as the physiological variable. These neural time series were multiplied by the onset times of HAP, HAN, LAP, LAN, and FIX separately and re-convolved with the canonical hemodynamic response function to obtain the PPI variables. The psychological regressors, physiological variable, and PPI variables were entered as regressors in a whole-brain GLM. Brain regions showing significant differences between BWS and CON were used as seed regions. Resulting positive contrast images were used in random-effect group analysis.

model_settings.value: Questionnaire responses of the BWS and CON groups were compared using independent samples t-tests.
